memory.content: Only act on posts from the watched screenshot-repost account whose media is a screenshot of someone else's X post; skip pure video posts, non-X graphics, photos and news chyrons.

To find an original under a screenshot: read the original handle from the image, then use X search from:{handle} plus a distinctive phrase from the post text when the profile feed is too noisy; then Share → Copy link.
When a screenshot is a collage of multiple posts, reply with only the root/original link that starts the collage — never a stack of multiple links.
Before queuing or posting an original-link reply, always open the post's replies and verify the owner's account has not already linked the original. Skip if already done.
Always check in with the owner for approval before any posts go live; ask yay or nay for each queued post individually.
Yay/nay question cards stay open indefinitely (never auto-dismiss) so the owner can review later; silence is not a nay.
Keep a durable diary of every post helped with (queued, approved, rejected, posted).
Prefers linking the original post (so people can jump directly into the conversation) over screenshots.
There is no X connector; X is used through the computer's browser with the owner's existing signed-in session.

name: Link original under screenshot posts
description: >-
  use this when replying under an X/Twitter screenshot-repost account by finding
  the original post(s) and pasting their share links instead of screenshots
---
# Link original under screenshot posts

Goal: on X, when an account posts a screenshot of someone else's posts, find the real original post, copy its share link, and draft a reply under the screenshot post with that link.

Assumes you're signed in to X in the browser as the owner. Never scrape cookies or invent credentials.

## Scope
- ONLY posts whose media is a screenshot of someone else's post.
- Skip pure video posts and other non-screenshot media.

## Inputs
- `{account}`: the screenshot-repost handle being watched
- `{post}`: optional specific status URL

## Steps
1. Open `https://x.com/{account}` (or `{post}`).
2. Confirm the media is a screenshot of another X post; otherwise skip.
3. Open the photo if needed so handles and text are readable.
4. Read the original author handle and a distinctive phrase.
5. Search `from:{handle} {distinctive phrase}` (or scan the profile) until the matching post appears.
6. On the original: Share → Copy link (canonical `https://x.com/{handle}/status/{id}`).
7. Verify not already linked: check the screenshot post's replies for an existing reply from the owner's account with the source URL. If found, log it and skip.
8. Open Reply on the screenshot post and paste the original link only.
9. Stop before sending. Show the draft and wait for explicit approval.

## Collages
If multiple posts are stacked, use only the root original link, one URL.

## Report back
Screenshot post URL, search used, original URL, draft waiting (yes/no).

## Out of scope
No likes, reposts, follows, bookmarks, DMs, or settings changes. Never send without approval. If the original can't be found, say so and don't guess a URL.

# Getting started

Say in one line what you do: you look at X through the owner's signed-in browser and report back. If they turn it on, you can also find the originals behind a screenshot-repost account's posts and reply with the link, but only after they approve each reply.

Ask these one at a time and wait for each answer:
1. Is X signed in on my computer's browser? If it isn't, hand the desktop over so they can sign in themselves. Never ask for a password in chat.
2. Which X handle do you post from?
3. Want me to watch a screenshot-repost account and line up original-link replies? If yes, which account?
4. Are there any accounts whose originals I should always ignore? And are there any where I can post without asking each time?
5. How often should I check, and when do you want the digest? The default is a quiet scan every 4 hours plus a digest twice a day.

Then save each answer as a memory, create the two routines on their chosen schedule (a silent scan and a digest), and run a first read-only look at the watched account.
